sentence: This project provides tissue and cell line banking and pathology services to help find ways to make a therapy work better against glioblastoma.
This project studies how the structure of the niche around stem cells lets it control the signals that stem cells receive.
This project builds an add-on module that lets standard clinical scanners do metabolic imaging of hyperpolarized compounds.
This project builds tools and shared resources for the Xiphophorus fish, a vertebrate used to study disease.
This project studies how citrate metabolism helps Staphylococcus aureus form biofilms and persist in prosthetic joint infections.
This project studies how a protein in liver macrophages affects liver cancer treatment.
This project builds digital twins that use genes, protein structure, cellular electrophysiology and electrocardiograms to predict disease and treatment for each patient.
This project studies how Legionella pneumophila survives and multiplies inside macrophages and changes the responses of host cells.
This project uses recordings and stimulation of the human brain to study how the posterior cingulate cortex supports episodic memory.
This project studies how brown adipocytes, which give off heat, help regulate energy expenditure and obesity.
This project tries to find out what makes a hematopoietic stem cell stay inactive or turn into different blood cells.
This project uses single-cell genomics and spatial transcriptomics to study how brain cell types respond to oxycodone in a rat model of addiction.
This project tries to find out how genetic variation leads to problems with neurotransmitter signaling in a pediatric disorder.
This project studies what the tumor suppressor protein p53 and its mutants do when cells change their fate, including in cancer.
This project develops therapeutic strategies that can be given hours to months after organophosphate exposure to reduce long-term harm to the brain.
This project studies how the Lyme disease bacterium Borrelia burgdorferi survives in tissues of mammals, particularly the skin.
This project provides mitochondrial function tests and high-resolution in vivo imaging to support research on cardiopulmonary diseases.
This project develops electrochemical and microfluidic methods to measure substances in cell spheroids and tissues that electrochemistry could not measure before.
This project studies how retrotransposon-derived promoters drive alternative gene versions during early development, using mouse genetics and sequencing.
This project studies how coenzyme A is made and controlled in mammalian and fly models, and how this relates to lipid metabolism.
